column3: Nearly repeats Iblis's declaration to mislead all and adds the earthly beautification strategy.
States the same immediate exception: Allah's purified servants lie outside Iblis's intended reach.
The messengers' warning removes excuses before the Mighty and Wise, only broadly framing accountable response.
Iblis declares that he will ambush people on the straight path, specifying the campaign behind his oath.
The request for reprieve is the immediate precondition for Iblis's subsequent pledge to mislead.
Its disputed attribution of misguidance to Allah is contrast-only and does not explain Iblis's agency here.
Misguided leaders admit that they misled others because they themselves were astray, directly showing the campaign's transmission.
The immediate continuation expressly excludes the purified servants from the universal target claimed at 38:82.
Allah's certain gathering of all people contrasts with Iblis's hostile attempt to draw all into misguidance.
It gives the declared outcome for Iblis and those who follow him: Hell filled with them all.
Private counsel after a failed negotiation does not clarify Iblis's oath, misguidance, or claimed totality.

Allah alone can gather every creature, providing a counterpoint to Iblis's claim over all people.
Allah's decisive proof and capacity to guide all delimit any claim that Iblis controls universal guidance.
The immediate conclusion turns Iblis's followers into the collective with whom Hell will be filled.

Iblis's arrogance and disbelief provide the immediate moral origin of his hostile pledge.

Creation of everything on earth for humanity does not clarify the focus reading.

The rescue of Lot's household as a whole does not clarify the oath or misguidance.

Abandoning prayer and following desires leads to deviation, showing a concrete path into error.

Musa and his companion retracing their steps does not illuminate the focus.
Charging into a gathered host shares no material relation with Iblis's project.

The failure of amassed numbers and arrogance offers only a distant warning against collective self-reliance.

The summons to congregational prayer does not clarify Iblis's misguidance campaign.
Iblis's refusal to prostrate is the foundational act of defiance behind his later oath.
Satan causes Adam and his spouse to slip, an early enactment of the misguidance he later pledges.
The warning not to follow Satan's steps identifies him as humanity's open enemy.
The command not to follow Satan's steps frames misguidance as a progressive course of allegiance.
Satan threatens poverty and commands indecency, specifying a concrete method of misleading people.

Satan frightens people through his allies, a defined tactic within his opposition to belief.
Satan seeks to lead claimants to faith far astray from revealed judgment.
The allies of Satan form the opposing allegiance whose plotting believers are told to resist.

Satan's promises and false hopes specify the deceptive means of his misguidance.
Intoxicants and gambling are described as Satan's work for turning people away from devotion.
Satan seeks enmity, hatred, and obstruction from Allah's remembrance and prayer.
Satan made prior nations' deeds seem fair, illustrating his strategy of deceptive beautification.
Devils among jinn and humans inspire embellished speech to deceive, a collective mechanism of misguidance.
Devils inspire their allies to dispute with believers, showing their influence through followers.
The command to prostrate and Iblis's refusal establish the immediate narrative setting of his rebellion.
Iblis justifies refusal through false superiority, exposing the pride driving his later hostility.
His expulsion for arrogance directly precedes his campaign against humanity.
Iblis requests respite until resurrection, the same enabling request answered in the focus passage.
Allah grants the respite that makes Iblis's subsequent misleading campaign possible.
Iblis declares his multi-directional assault on people so that many will not be grateful.
Satan whispers to Adam and his spouse and makes temptation appear beneficial.
He reinforces temptation with a false oath, a direct counterpart to his oath at 38:82.
Satan deceives the pair by delusion, showing the successful operation of his temptation.
Satan's temptation of Adam and his spouse warns believers not to be similarly deceived.
One who follows Satan becomes among the astray, directly linking Satanic following to misguidance.
The command to seek refuge at Satanic incitement recognizes his active pressure on people.
The mindful remember Allah when touched by Satan and regain sight, marking a counter to his influence.
Satan beautifies deeds, promises protection, and then abandons his followers at confrontation.
Satan is named an open enemy who could exploit Yusuf's dream through his brothers.
Satan admits that he only called people, disowns them, and distinguishes his false promise from Allah's true one.

Allah questions Iblis's refusal, directly developing the reason for his rebellious posture.
Iblis asserts superiority over Adam, exposing the pride that grounds his later vow.
Allah expels Iblis, the judgment that frames his adversarial campaign.
The curse upon Iblis until the Day of Judgment provides the punitive setting for his oath.

Believers are instructed to seek refuge from the accursed Satan when reciting the Qur'an.
Satan has no authority over those who believe and rely on their Lord, delimiting his claimed reach.
His authority extends only to those who take him as patron and associate partners with Allah.
Satan seeks to sow discord among people, a social tactic within his enmity.
Iblis refuses to prostrate to Adam and challenges the honor granted to him.
Iblis threatens to seize Adam's descendants, except a few, closely paralleling the universal target at 38:82.
Allah identifies Hell as the recompense for Iblis and those who follow him.
Iblis is authorized to entice with voice, mobilize followers, share wealth and children, and make promises.
Allah denies Iblis authority over sincere servants, directly matching the exception at 38:83.
Iblis disobeys his Lord's command and is identified as an enemy whose offspring people must not take as protectors.
Abraham warns that serving Satan means following a rebellious adversary of the Most Merciful.
Iblis refuses the command to prostrate, the central primal act of defiance.
Satan whispers to Adam with the lure of permanence and undying dominion.

Some people follow every rebellious Satan without knowledge, identifying his susceptible followers.
Whoever takes Satan as patron is led astray by him and directed toward the Blaze.

Seeking refuge from the devils' presence recognizes their active, harmful approach.
Following Satan's steps leads toward indecency and wrongdoing, while Allah's grace purifies.
Satan leads a person away from the Reminder and then abandons him.
Satan makes the sun-worshippers' deeds seem fair and bars them from the path.
Satan makes former peoples' deeds attractive and obstructs them from the path.

Satan is declared an enemy who calls his party to become companions of the Blaze.
Allah's covenant forbids worship of Satan and names him humanity's clear enemy.

Turning from the Most Merciful's remembrance results in a devil assigned as an intimate companion.
Those devils turn people from the path while the people suppose themselves guided.
Satan entices those who turn back after guidance and fills them with false hopes.
Satan overcomes his party and makes them forget Allah's remembrance; they are explicitly his party.
Satan induces disbelief, then disowns the person once disbelief occurs.
